The short-interval maximum conjecture uses a logarithmically correlated field and predicts a −(3/4) log log log T correction to log log T on the zeta side. The freezing heuristic, Toeplitz-moment comparison and finite-height experiments are distinguished from a theorem about zeta maxima.

Theorem 1.2 extends Fujii’s mesoscopic CLT to compactly supported real bounded-variation test functions with divergent integral of |x||η̂(x)|². Assuming RH, the upper bound for the 2kth critical-line moment has the sharp order \(T(\log T)^{k^2}\) for every fixed real \(k\ge0\). Adaptive prime-block lengths remove the extra logarithmic loss from the earlier Soundararajan approach.

For Haar U(N), the full-circle maximum of the log modulus divided by log N tends to 1 in probability. The high-point set at level γ log N has logarithmic measure exponent −γ² for fixed 0<γ<1. These are matrix-ensemble results.

Theorem 1.1 gives an unconditional leading scale log log T for the maximum of log |ζ| over |t−u|≤1 for a proportion tending to one of t in [T,2T]. It records independent conditional work by Najnudel and does not establish the FHK second-order law.

Theorem 1 supplies the upper tail C y exp(−2y) at level eʸ log T/(log log T)^{3/4}, uniformly for T≥3 and y≥1, for the maximum over |h|≤1 about a uniformly random t in [T,2T]. Theorem 1 bounds the probability of the maximum falling below e⁻ʸ log T/(log log T)^{3/4} by c⁻¹y⁻ᶜ for 0<y≤(log log T)^{1/10}, T≥100. Paired with Part I this gives tightness of the recentered maximum, which is weaker than identifying its limiting law.

Theorem 1.2 gives an upper tail refined by the Gaussian factor exp(−y²/((1+θ)log log T)) for fixed −1<θ≤0 and y between 2 and C log log T/log log log T. The critical-line radius is (log T)^θ, with the low-prime factor Pτ(θ) multiplying the maximum. Theorem 1.3 concerns the normalized second-moment partition function.

Theorem 1.1 gives an unconditional lower bound by a positive α-dependent multiple of the Gaussian tail for V∼α log log T, every fixed α>0. It complements the existing separate upper bounds and also treats primitive even characters of prime conductor at central points in Theorem 1.3.

Theorem 2.1 states an unconditional Gumbel limit with scale 1/(2√(1+θ)), fixed θ>0, about a uniform random height in [T,2T]. Its interval radius is (log T)^θ and its real part moves to 1/2 from the right under the prime-power cutoff and displacement hypotheses in (2.1). Centering uses an exact upper quantile in the auxiliary Haar model. This is a distinct regime from the critical-line maximum.
